question.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloid $x={y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}$ and the parabolic cylinder $x=3-2{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{a(y)}^{b(y)}\,f(y,z)\,dz\,dy
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $yz$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2} & =3-2{y}^{2} \\ 3{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $yz$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type II region: 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}\le x\le 3-2{y}^{2}\},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $3{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}=3.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}}^{3-2{y}^{2}}\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3-2{y}^{2})-({y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3-3{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{2}},$

for $-1\le y\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}3-3{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{3(1-{y}^{2})/2}}^{\sqrt{3(1-{y}^{2})/2}}\,3-3{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{2}})}^{2}+(3-3{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{2}+\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{2}+(3-3{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}) \\  & =6-6{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
